findings.title: Adoption accepts unbound intermediate commits and hidden tracked paths
findings.reproduction: At candidate 060899b5ec438003ad188d3be21da1f29b8d3908, tools/gcrctl.py command_adopt checks only that --approved-state-commit equals HEAD^ and is ancestral to HEAD. It does not prove that this parent is the canonical commit applying the latest APPROVED ledger/state, does not constrain the reviewed-state-to-approved-state delta, and does not compare the complete approved-state-to-evidence-commit diff to the single canonical adoption-evidence path. A temporary real-Git replay subclassed the shipped happy-path lifecycle test so that planning/unauthorized-hidden.txt was added beside artifacts/evidence/governance-control-recovery/GCR-0001.B00.adoption.json in the evidence commit. The unchanged controller printed the 6-to-7 adoption success and the test passed with hidden_extra_commit_accepted=True. The shipped test inspects only the uncommitted post-command diff, so it cannot detect the already committed extra path. This violates the exact ancestry/path authority, hidden-extra-path denial, and direct-child adoption boundary required by acceptance criterion 8 and verification obligation 4.
findings.requiredRemediation: In a strict-descendant candidate, derive rather than trust the canonical latest reviewed-state and approved-state commits. Require the APPROVED ledger/state application to have the exact permitted status/path delta and ancestry, require the pre-adoption evidence commit to be its direct child with exactly one added canonical adoption-evidence file and no add/delete/rename/copy/type-change/substitution/omission/extra path, and verify that file's exact Git blob/hash. Add isolated real-Git denial tests for hidden paths and intermediate/substituted commits at both boundaries while preserving the append-only R01 finding and using fresh R02 evidence with an explicit closure.

findings.title: The two-file adoption writer is not interruption-atomic
findings.reproduction: tools/gcrctl.py atomic_adoption_write prepares two temporary files and then calls os.replace sequentially for planning/backlog.yaml and the canonical GCR state. Its exception handler can restore bytes only while the process remains alive. An independent child-process probe forced os._exit(77) immediately after the first real replacement; the child terminated with 77 and partial_write_observed=True: backlog bytes had advanced while GCR state bytes remained APPROVED. No durable transaction marker or startup recovery exists. Moreover, command_validate selects the revision from the backlog and validate_state_history accepts an APPROVED state with no adoption record, so the resulting revision-7/APPROVED split is not expressly rejected. The shipped affected suite has an exception-path atomic-save test for a different single-file writer but no abrupt-interruption GCR adoption test. This violates acceptance criterion 6, the required byte-stable/atomic failure behavior, and the prohibition on weakening atomic persistence.
findings.requiredRemediation: Implement an interruption-safe two-record adoption protocol that either exposes both successor records or preserves/restores both predecessor records across process termination, and make every reader fail closed on or deterministically recover any prepared/partial combination. Bind the transaction to the exact expected backlog/state bytes and approved evidence commit, fsync the required files/directories on Windows as appropriate, and add child-process abrupt-termination tests at every persistence boundary plus stale/concurrent failure tests proving byte-stable predecessor state or a fully consistent successor. Preserve this R01 finding append-only and close it only with fresh R02 evidence from a strict-descendant candidate.

findings.title: The final adoption commit and recovery workspace remain outside the exact path boundary
findings.reproduction: The strict-descendant candidate correctly constrains candidate-to-REVIEW, REVIEW-to-disposition, and approved-state-to-adoption-evidence commits, but neither gcrctl nor taskctl derives and validates the later commit that records the canonical ADOPTED state and revision-7 backlog. In a temporary real-Git lifecycle, the remediated controller completed adoption; the resulting backlog and state were then committed together with planning/hidden-final-adoption.txt. The commit's name/status delta was M planning/backlog.yaml, M planning/governance-control-recovery/GCR-0001.B00.state.json, and A planning/hidden-final-adoption.txt, yet gcrctl.validate_state_history returned successfully and hidden_final_adoption_commit_accepted=True. A second temporary lifecycle stopped immediately after transaction publication, created unrelated-untracked.tmp, and invoked recover_adoption_transaction. Recovery returned COMPLETED_SUCCESSOR while the unrelated file survived, producing dirty_recovery_accepted=True. recover checks branch, trigger witness, transaction authority, and canonical record hashes, but it does not deny unrelated staged, tracked-worktree, or untracked paths. These paths can therefore coexist with completion of the exact governance transition, contrary to acceptance criterion 8's direct-child exactly-two-path adoption commit, the packet's every-extra-path denial, and its clean Git identity prohibition.
findings.requiredRemediation: In a strict-descendant R03 candidate, add a non-circular finalization invariant that derives the unique commit introducing the adopted backlog/state pair, requires it to be the direct child of the exact adoption-evidence commit, requires the complete no-renames name/status delta to be exactly M planning/backlog.yaml and M planning/governance-control-recovery/GCR-0001.B00.state.json, and verifies both Git blobs against the live successor bytes before any adopted generation is accepted by gcrctl or taskctl. Before that commit exists, expose only a fail-closed pending-finalization state and deny downstream recovery-supplement use. Add a specialized recovery workspace guard that permits only the hash-bound trigger witness, the exact canonical transaction artifacts, and canonical backlog/state bytes at a declared predecessor/successor boundary; deny every other untracked path, every staged path, and every unrelated tracked worktree change before cleanup or roll-forward. Add real-Git tests for hidden/substituted final adoption commits and for untracked, staged, and unrelated tracked dirty recovery attempts. Preserve R01 and R02 append-only, submit fresh R03 evidence, and explicitly close this finding before revision 7 is usable.

findings.title: The exact preceding reader accepts a hidden-path adoption finalization
findings.reproduction: Load tools/taskctl.py from the exact preceding R02 candidate 22f9b46dd6772d2df615d3324cd1797f585385f8 and execute its governance_control_generation_errors against an otherwise valid real-Git GCR approval, review, and adoption lifecycle. Commit the adopted backlog and state as the direct child of the adoption-evidence commit together with A planning/hidden-final-adoption.txt. The current R03 reader returns GCR-0001 adoption finalization commit is not the exact two-path transition, while the exact R02 reader returns an empty error list. R03 adds the finalization check without a successor-state or control marker that the already revision-8 R02 reader rejects; the submitted older-reader test only patches the current implementation to revision 6 and therefore does not exercise this immediate predecessor. The hidden path can consequently be accepted by a supported stale taskctl path, contradicting criteria 2 and 8, the packet's old-reader fail-closed rule, and the R03 claim that the exact direct-child boundary is enforced in current and older readers.
findings.requiredRemediation: In a strict-descendant R04 candidate, add a canonical, packet-consistent successor-state or tool-generation marker that the exact R02 taskctl reader fails closed on and that the current gcrctl/taskctl readers require before accepting revision 7. Do not rely only on a new optional field that the old reader ignores or on a simulated revision-6 constant. Add a real-Git regression that loads the exact R02 taskctl implementation and proves it rejects an otherwise valid revision-7 adoption containing a hidden finalization path, while the current reader accepts only the exact direct-child two-path finalization. Preserve all prior attempts and submit fresh evidence with an explicit closure for this finding.

findings.title: Finalization proof is coupled to the mutable live backlog and fails after lawful evolution
findings.reproduction: In a temporary real-Git lifecycle, complete an otherwise valid GCR adoption, commit the exact direct-child two-path finalization, and call governance_control_adoption_finalization_errors with the live state and backlog bytes; it returns an empty list. Then make a later backlog-only commit representing subsequent lawful control evolution and call the same helper with the unchanged adopted state and the new live backlog bytes; it returns GCR-0001 adoption is pending its exact finalization commit. The helper searches history for a state-path-changing commit whose backlog blob equals the current live backlog, so any later authorized backlog evolution, including the separately gated GRR-0002.S01 7-to-8 supplement required by criterion 4, makes the immutable revision-7 finalization undiscoverable. Current gcrctl and taskctl will then reject the otherwise valid generation history indefinitely.
findings.requiredRemediation: In the same strict-descendant candidate, derive the unique direct-child finalization from the immutable adoption-evidence commit and validate that commit's own exact two-path delta and revision-7 backlog/state blobs, rather than comparing its backlog blob to mutable live backlog bytes. Validate later live backlog revisions through their separately authorized append-only supplement/generation transitions. Add a real-Git test that proves exact revision-7 finalization remains valid after a lawful later backlog transition, including the revision-7-to-8 boundary required for GRR-0002.S01, while hidden, substituted, omitted, duplicated, and unrelated finalization commits still fail closed.

closures.evidence: Candidate d94ec5a5fef01fe425b7bc0d784d5915a46ab4db closes the R02 reproduction in the current reader and adds an exact recovery-workspace guard: the current reader rejects hidden and substituted finalization commits, and unrelated untracked, staged, or tracked recovery state is denied with byte stability. Independent replay nevertheless found two narrower blocking boundaries not isolated in R02: the exact preceding R02 taskctl reader accepts the hidden-path finalization, and the immutable finalization becomes undiscoverable after later lawful backlog evolution.
